name: Report a fractured well to the customer
summary: After each well is fractured the company sends the producer a treatment report (stage-by-stage volumes, rates, pressures and proppant placed, with charts and a narrative of events) and the chemical data the producer needs for its fracturing fluid disclosure. The data van technician cleans and exports the stage data, the treater writes the report, and a completions design engineer in Calgary checks it against the design and turns the products pumped into ingredient concentrations for the disclosure. Delays come from treaters on rotation, engineers reviewing in batches and suppliers slow to release confidential ingredient data, and the producer's 30-day disclosure deadline sets the limit.

baseline.org_archetype: A TSX-listed Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight 24-hour frac crews working for producers in Alberta and northeast BC, run from district bases with a Calgary head office.
baseline.notes: Modelled on the organisation file oilfield-services-co (composite based on Trican and STEP Canada). 2020 was a deep downturn and sits at the low end of volume ranges.

unit_of_work: one well report (treatment report and fluid disclosure data for one fractured well)
trigger: Job execution sends the well's treatment data after its last stage is pumped.
end_state: The producer has the final treatment report and the chemical disclosure data for the well, has accepted them, and both are filed in the job folder; the data are with technical services for analysis.

volume.seasonality: One report per well fractured, so it follows frac activity with a lag of one to two weeks.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same surge as the organisation file's process map entry (crews fully booked January to mid-March); the multiplier is an estimate from quarterly proppant swings of 260,000-479,000 tonnes in the organisation file.
Equal to wells fractured (organisation file driver frac-wells).
Organisation file headcount 26; data export, QC and charts for each well (estimate).
Organisation file headcount 24; writes the treatment report and narrative (estimate).

Organisation file headcount 16; reviews reports and prepares fluid disclosure data for about 50 wells a month (estimate). Some companies give the disclosure work to an HSE or regulatory coordinator instead.

systems.name: Data van acquisition and treatment monitoring system
Fracture and cement placement modelling software
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Laboratory test records (lab database and spreadsheets)

steps.name: Close the well's job file in the data van
steps.description: After the last stage the data van technician closes the well's acquisition file, checks every stage is saved under the right well and stage number, and backs the file up to the server.

error.defect_description: A stage is saved under the wrong well or number.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Check the stage data for gaps and sensor errors
steps.description: The technician scrolls through each stage looking for gaps, flat-lined or spiking sensors, wrong densometer readings and unit mix-ups, and compares totals with the stage summaries the wellsite supervisor signed.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Rebuild gaps from backup or paper records
steps.description: Where acquisition dropped out the technician fills the gap from the backup recorder, the blender's own log or the paper sheets, and flags the reconstructed section in the file.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Produce stage charts and summary tables
steps.description: The technician runs the report template in the acquisition software to produce a pressure, rate and concentration chart for every stage and a table of volumes, average and maximum pressures, breakdown and ISIP by stage.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Gather chemical volumes from blender records and tote counts
steps.description: The technician pulls the volume of each additive pumped per stage from the blender log and checks the totals against the blender operator's chemical reconciliation and tote counts.

error.defect_description: Additive volumes in the report do not match the tote counts.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Write the treatment report and narrative
steps.description: The treater fills in the report template: well and design details, stage table, proppant and fluid totals against design, chemicals, and a narrative of events such as screen-outs, cut stages and stoppages, with the NPT reports attached.

error.defect_description: A narrative item or total is wrong or missing.

evidence.note: The wait reflects treaters writing between wells on the next pad or after their rotation; estimate.

steps.name: Send the field copy to the wellsite supervisor
steps.description: The treater emails the draft report and charts to the customer's wellsite supervisor and completion engineer as the field copy, so they can start their own completion records.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Upload the report and data to the job folder
steps.description: The technician copies the report, charts and raw data to the well's job folder on the document server, where technical services pick them up for analysis and the design engineer for review.

error.defect_description: A file is missing from the folder.

evidence.note: Post-job data delivered to clients through an online tool in STEP's practice; time estimated.

steps.name: Review the report against the design
steps.description: A completions design engineer in Calgary compares the report with the design: proppant placed by stage, fluid volumes, pressures and chemical loadings, checks the totals against the field ticket and sends back anything that does not add up.

evidence.note: Engineers review reports in batches between design work; wait estimated.

steps.name: Correct the report
steps.description: The treater fixes the totals or narrative the engineer queried, often after checking with the data technician, and sends the report back.

evidence.note: The wait reflects field rotation (treaters away on days off); estimate.

steps.name: Map products to ingredients and CAS numbers
steps.description: The engineer looks up each product pumped on the safety data sheets and the company's product list to get its ingredients, CAS numbers and maximum mass fractions.

error.defect_description: An ingredient or CAS number is taken from an outdated data sheet.

next.condition: a supplier product has undisclosed ingredients

evidence.note: Disclosure content as in common practice; the FracFocus page opened describes the registry but not its data fields.

steps.name: Ask the chemical supplier for confidential ingredient data
steps.description: For a third-party product with ingredients withheld as trade secrets, the engineer emails the supplier for the ingredient list or a confirmation that it will claim confidentiality with the regulator.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Supplier provides the ingredient data or a confidentiality claim
steps.description: The supplier's regulatory staff send the ingredient breakdown under a confidentiality agreement, or confirm that they will claim trade-secret status with the regulator, so the engineer can finish the disclosure.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Calculate maximum ingredient concentrations in the fluid
steps.description: The engineer uses the volumes of water, proppant and each additive pumped to calculate each ingredient's maximum concentration in the total fluid by mass, in a spreadsheet.

error.defect_description: A unit conversion or water volume is wrong.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Fill in the disclosure template with water volumes and sources
steps.description: The engineer copies the concentrations, total water volume and water source the customer gave into the producer's disclosure template, ready for the producer to submit to the registry and the regulator.

error.defect_description: A value is copied into the wrong row.

evidence.note: Alberta disclosure records include water volumes and sources (FracFocus.ca).

steps.name: Second engineer checks the disclosure
steps.description: Another engineer checks the ingredient list and concentrations against the report and data sheets before anything goes to the producer.

control.basis: Company second-check rule for regulatory data supplied to customers

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Send the disclosure and final report to the producer
steps.description: The engineer emails the final treatment report and the disclosure file to the producer's completion engineer and regulatory contact, in time for the producer to submit within 30 days of finishing completion operations.

control.basis: Fracturing fluid disclosure within 30 days of the end of completion operations (FracFocus.ca, AER Directive 059); a licensee duty the service company supplies data for

evidence.note: 30-day submission window (FracFocus.ca); licensees file well data under Directive 059.

steps.name: Producer reviews the report and disclosure
steps.description: The producer's completion engineer and regulatory staff check the report and disclosure against their own records and either accept them, send questions, or ask for extra analysis.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Answer the producer's query
steps.description: The engineer checks the producer's query against the stage data and data sheets, then corrects and resends the report or disclosure, or replies explaining how the figure was calculated.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the extra analysis the customer asked for
steps.description: For some customers the engineer adds analysis such as net pressure matching, step-down test results or comparisons with offset wells, using the design software and the stage data.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: File the final report and disclosure in the job folder
steps.description: The engineer saves the accepted versions in the job folder, marks the well's report complete on the tracking sheet and lets technical services know the data are final.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Data gaps
exceptions.description: Acquisition dropouts are patched from backups or paper.

exceptions.name: Report corrections
exceptions.description: The engineer sends the report back to the treater.

exceptions.name: Supplier ingredient data
exceptions.description: Confidential ingredients must be obtained from a supplier.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from last stage to accepted report and disclosure

evidence.note: Estimate bounded by the producer's 30-day disclosure window (FracFocus.ca): the service company has to deliver well inside it, leaving the producer time to submit.

benchmarks.unit: days after the end of completion operations

pain_points.description: Treaters write reports between wells or after their rotation, and engineers review them in batches, so most of the elapsed time is queueing.

evidence.note: Field rotation and batching of engineering reviews are the author's description of common practice.

pain_points.description: Chemical volumes are copied by hand from the blender log into the report and then into the disclosure, and mismatches with tote counts are found late.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Third-party products with confidential ingredients wait on supplier regulatory staff and push against the producer's 30-day window.

evidence.note: 30-day window from FracFocus.ca; supplier delays estimated.

sources.title: Case Study: Increasing Pumping Hours Through Optimized Operations - STEP Energy Services
sources.supports: Canadian frac pads: average pumping hours per day rose from 14.03 (Q4 2018, three pads) to 18.93 on a four-well pad for one client, and from 15.47 (February 2019) to 17.95 (August 2019) for another; gains from managing maintenance schedules, bi-weekly meetings with operators and pre- and post-pad reviews; post-job data delivered to clients through an online tool.

sources.title: FracFocus.ca - Hydraulic Fracturing Chemical Registry
sources.supports: Companies undertaking hydraulic fracturing in British Columbia (wells fractured from 1 January 2012) and Alberta (from 1 January 2013) submit fluid records within 30 days of the end of completion operations; Alberta records include water volumes and sources.

sources.title: Directive 059: Well Drilling and Completion Data Filing Requirements
sources.supports: Directive on completing and submitting daily operations records and well data in a timely manner through the Digital Data Submission system, with related guidance on hydraulic fracture fluid data.

assumptions: The design engineer prepares the disclosure data; in some companies an HSE or regulatory coordinator does it from the same records.
The producer, not the service company, submits the disclosure to FracFocus.ca and the AER; this workflow ends when the producer accepts the data.
The wait before the treater writes the report covers field rotation: a treater who finishes a pad on the last day of a hitch may write it a week later.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (base wage x 1.35).
